items.title: Thousands await aid after Indonesia quake kills 51
items.summary: RUTENG, Indonesia: Help started arriving Sunday for thousands of evacuees on Indonesia's Flores island after a powerful earthquake killed 51 people, injured dozens and damaged hundreds of houses and buildings. Some 5,000 people fled their homes as the 7.7-magnitude quake hit the island early Saturday, followed by at least 341 aftershocks in the hours that followed, a spokesman for the BNPB national disaster agency, Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan, said. People in some areas were left without electricity and telecommunications and at least one emergency access road remained inaccessible.

items.title: Malaysia braces for stronger El Nino, worsening transboundary haze
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government is bracing for a stronger El Nino and the possibility of a more severe wave of transboundary haze as prolonged hot and dry conditions increase the risk of fires across the region. He said the ministry was taking seriously the haze situation that has affected Sarawak, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya since Aug 8. However, he said conditions in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya had improved.

items.title: Sara to continue despite country facing current global economic challenges – Amir Hamzah
items.summary: TAWAU: Efforts to provide assistance to the people through the Basic Rahmah Contribution (Sara) programme remain the government's priority in preparing the 2027 Budget despite the current challenging global economic environment, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. He said the government through the budget would continue to provide allocation space for the targeted cash assistance programme next year to ease the burden of the people's cost of living, especially the needy. Amir Hamzah said the Sara programme has proven effective as the total allocation for Sara and the Rahmah Cash Contribution this year reached RM15 billion.

items.title: Jakarta team to brief NCID top brass this week on pilot drug case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Bukit Aman team sent to Jakarta to interview a Malaysia Airlines pilot detained in a major drug trafficking case will brief the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) top brass this week on leads uncovered during three days of questioning. NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the team returned to Malaysia on Saturday (Aug 15) after interviewing the 39-year-old pilot in Jakarta from Aug 12 to 14. The NCID team travelled to Jakarta on Aug 11 with the cooperation of Indonesian police to interview the pilot, who was arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on July 28.

items.title: Merdeka Month: Taking responsibility for our future
items.summary: LETTER: Every August, Malaysians proudly celebrate Merdeka Month, a time when we commemorate our nation's independence and pay tribute to the sacrifices of our founding fathers and all those who fought tirelessly to secure our freedom. As Malaysia approaches another National Day, we must ask ourselves an important question: What does Merdeka mean to Malaysians today? Yet true independence goes beyond political freedom.

items.title: USM leaps 149 places to lead Malaysia in global university ranking
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) has emerged as Malaysia's top university in the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) 2026. Also known as the ShanghaiRanking, ARWU evaluates universities based on academic and research performance rather than reputation or perception alone. Its performance in the Highly Cited Researchers indicator also improved to No 503 globally.

items.title: 12 killed as Polish bus overturns in Hungary
items.summary: BUDAPEST: A Polish bus overturned on a Hungarian highway early Sunday killing 12 people and leaving at least 10 with serious injuries, Prime Minister Peter Magyar and officials said. The ambulance service said 37 people suffered minor injuries. In 2002, a bus carrying Polish pilgrims crashed near the western town of Balatonszentgyorgy (ouest) killing 19 people.

items.title: Businessman's body found in net: One suspect also faces firearms charge
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: One of four suspects who will be charged tomorrow over the alleged murder of a businessman whose body was found wrapped in a net is also facing a firearms possession charge. "One of the suspects will also be charged under Section 8 of the Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act 1971. Ab Rahaman said checks found that one of the two suspects had a previous criminal record.

items.title: PM Anwar vows full repeal of AUKU, no replacement laws curbing student freedom or movement
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — The government has given an assurance that the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) will be fully repealed without introducing any new laws that restrict or suppress student movements. “I also do not agree with any amendment or replacement (law) that restricts or suppresses student activities,” said Anwar, who is also PKR president. “Students are ordinary citizens.

items.title: Weather warning: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit 10 states and the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya until 6pm today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the affected areas include Perlis; Kedah (Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena, Kota Setar, Sik, Baling and Pendang); and Perak (Hulu Perak). The warning also covers Kelantan (Gua Musang); Terengganu (Kemaman, Dungun, Hulu Terengganu, Marang and Kuala Terengganu); Pahang (Cameron Highlands, Bera, Rompin, Pekan and Jerantut); and Selangor (Hulu Langat, Sepang, Petaling, Gombak and Kuala Langat).

items.title: Dungun doctor duped in forex, Ethereum scam, loses RM558,000 through 77 transactions
items.summary: DUNGUN, Aug 16 — A female doctor at a private clinic here lost RM558,000 after falling victim to an online forex and Ethereum coin investment scam since January. Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the 32-year-old victim initially saw an advertisement offering trading and investment lessons before contacting an individual via Instagram. District police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the 60-year-old victim responded to a Facebook advertisement in June offering loans with low interest rates and attractive terms.

items.title: Pas open to seat swaps with Umno in upcoming elections
items.summary: TEMERLOH: Pas is prepared to consider swapping its incumbent state and parliamentary seats with Umno, subject to certain conditions in upcoming elections, deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said. Any proposed seat exchange should generally involve a 'win seat for win seat' or 'losing seat' arrangement. Pahang Umno liaison chief Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail subsequently said Umno was open to cooperating with any political party, including Pas.

items.title: Malaysia's growth forecasts lifted after stronger Q2
items.summary: Kenanga Research raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5.3 per cent from 4.5-5.0 per cent, while MBSB Research lifted its projection to 5.1 per cent from 4.5 per cent. Meanwhile, RHB Research maintained its 2026 GDP growth forecast at 5.4 per cent, above the government's official projection of 4.0-4.5 per cent and Bank Negara Malaysia's forecast range of 4.0 to 5.0 per cent. JPMorgan had earlier raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5.3 per cent from 5.0 per cent on July 21, following the stronger-than-expected Q2 advance estimate.

items.title: Nurul Izzah urges continuous reform within PKR and government
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar has called for reform to be pursued continuously within the party as well as in government administration and policies. She said the party's struggle, born from the reform movement, must not end upon entering government but continue as a legacy for future generations. "That is why we cannot stop fighting just because we are in government; instead, party members must continue to carry out reform continuously," she said.

items.title: Diesel subsidy shake‑up coming soon; govt promises simpler rules, family quota transfers, easier access
items.summary: TAWAU, Aug 16 — Several improvements to the implementation of the targeted diesel subsidy system are being studied, with the government expected to announce them within the next one to two months, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. Amir Hamzah said preparations for the 2027 Budget would ensure more effective and comprehensive delivery of assistance to the people under the targeted diesel subsidy. “Through the 2027 Budget Tour series, we are examining various improvements to the targeted diesel subsidy mechanism to ensure that those who are truly eligible can benefit from it optimally,” he said.

items.title: Nurul Izzah: I remain committed to same reform spirit since 1998
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar remains committed to the same spirit of struggle that drove the reform movement when it began in 1998, Sinar Harian reported today. According to the report, Nurul Izzah said although she would carry out her responsibilities through a different avenue in the future, her goals remained the same — strengthening institutions, preserving dignity and creating more opportunities for Malaysians. “PKR will continue to carry this responsibility.

items.title: 25 undocumented migrants fined up to RM10,000 for immigration offences
items.summary: The group, comprising 16 Bangladeshi men, four Indonesian men, three Indonesian women and two Cambodian men, were among 26 foreigners brought before the court to face charges. Twelve of the Bangladeshi men were charged under Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for overstaying, while the remaining four were charged under Section 6(1)(c) of the same Act for entering or remaining in Malaysia without a valid pass or permit. The two Cambodian men, four Indonesian men and three Indonesian women were also charged with overstaying.

items.title: Three arrested after woman allegedly punched over illegal parking fees in OUG
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested three men after a 38-year-old woman was allegedly punched in the head and threatened when she confronted them over illegal parking fee collection in OUG. Police later arrested three men, aged between 20 and 26. Fadil said checks found all three had previous criminal records.

items.title: PKR leaders vow fairness for all races, slam racial propaganda, urge unity over ego
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — PKR must continue to defend a fair political approach to all sections of society, while respecting the position of Islam and the Malays in the Federal Constitution. PKR vice president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the position of Islam and the Malays is a core element in the Federal Constitution that must be respected by all parties. In line with Amirudin, PKR vice president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan wanted PKR to remain firm in defending the diversity of races in this country and strongly reject actions that use racial issues as political capital.

items.title: Police arrest two suspects in Salak South temple assault case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested two men over an alleged assault that left a man unconscious with severe injuries near a temple in Salak South in April. Cheras district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said the suspects, in their early 30s, were detained around Razak City Residences yesterday. "The incident was reported on April 9, when a local man in his late 20s was found unconscious near a temple in Salak South.

items.title: 2027 Budget to focus on Sabah's blue economy
items.summary: TAWAU: Sabah's marine and aquaculture sectors will receive special focus in the preparation of 2027 Budget as the government identifies the Blue Economy as a new strategic area to drive economic growth. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the Federal government is working closely with the Sabah state government to ensure the sector is developed effectively for the benefit of the people. He said Sabah has strong potential to lead in marine and aquaculture industries, prompting the government to engage with industry players during the 2027 Budget engagement session here today.

items.title: 20 undocumented migrants detained in separate Kelantan maritime operations
items.summary: PASIR PUTEH: The cover of darkness may have helped migrant smugglers evade a maritime patrol boat, but their movements along Sungai Kelantan eventually led enforcement officers to 20 foreigners believed to have entered the country illegally. The Kelantan Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) intercepted two groups of undocumented migrants in separate operations this week involving foreigners from India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia and Myanmar. Kelantan Maritime director Kepten Maritim Kamal Mohamad said both operations began after the agency received intelligence about attempts to use unauthorised routes along the river to bring migrants into the country.

items.title: All 14 delegates debate in favour of DAP remaining in Cabinet ahead of secret ballot
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: All 14 delegates who took the floor to debate the motion on DAP's future in the unity government spoke in favour of remaining in the Cabinet, urging fellow delegates to vote for continued cooperation in the administration. Kedah delegate Lim Hooi Yee said DAP should not punish the unity government over what she described as a marginal electoral defeat in recent state elections. Do not let our party become merely the government's spokesperson to the people.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar: PKR to remain aligned with BN-Umno while staying loyal to PH partners
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR will continue working with Barisan Nasional and Umno at the federal level while remaining committed to Pakatan Harapan partners DAP and Amanah, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. The PKR president said the decision to maintain cooperation with BN-Umno was made to preserve political stability for the economy, while stressing that PKR would remain loyal to its partners in PH. So I say, we must remain together," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress here.

items.title: Anwar says any decision on Umno must prioritise people’s welfare, ‘not anger’
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Prime Minister and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told party delegates today that he chose to put the people first, amid growing internal censure against the party’s unity government ally Barisan Nasional. Speaking at this year’s congress, Anwar said any decision regarding PKR’s cooperation with BN and Umno must not be driven by anger, but instead treated carefully through what he described as political “wisdom” that ultimately puts national interests above partisan conflicts. “It must always be driven by public and national interests.

items.title: Anwar launches Temu Fikrah publication at PKR National Congress
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Prime Minister and Parti Keadilan Rakyat president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched Temu Fikrah, a book published by PKR Youth at the 2026 PKR National Congress. The 113-page publication, authored by Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Ahmad Munim and executive committee member Ashraf Ahmad Hadi, outlines the movement's new thinking on addressing contemporary challenges. In the foreword, Anwar described the publication as timely, coinciding with the adoption of the Malaysia Madani concept as the intellectual framework and strategic direction for the nation's administration.

items.title: Saifuddin: Needs-based aid will benefit Malays most
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Malays will remain the biggest beneficiaries of government aid even if it is distributed based on need rather than race, PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today. He said poverty affected all ethnic groups and aid should therefore be channelled based on need, not race. There are poor Malays, poor Chinese, poor Indians, Ibans and Kadazans.

items.title: Woman punched, threatened in OUG parking row; KL police arrest three suspects with records (VIDEO)
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 16 — Police have arrested three men after a woman reported being assaulted and threatened during an alleged illegal parking fee collection near the OUG community hall in Jalan Awan Besar. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said three suspects, aged between 20 and 26, were detained following the incident. Police urged the public to report any information on crime to the Brickfields police hotline at 03 22979222, the Kuala Lumpur hotline at 03 21159999, or the nearest police station.

items.title: Targeted diesel subsidy system improvements expected in 1-2 months - Amir Hamzah
items.summary: TAWAU: Several improvements to the implementation of the targeted diesel subsidy system are being studied, with the government expected to announce them within the next one to two months, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. Amir Hamzah said preparations for the Budget 2027 would ensure more effective and comprehensive delivery of assistance to the people under the targeted diesel subsidy. "Through the Budget 2027 Tour series, we are examining various improvements to the targeted diesel subsidy mechanism to ensure that those who are truly eligible can benefit from it optimally ," he said.

items.title: Anwar's 79th birthday celebrated as PKR National Congress concludes in Ayer Keroh
items.summary: AYER KEROH: The 2026 PKR National Congress concluded today with a celebration of party president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's 79th birthday, attended by over 2,000 delegates and observers. Anwar, who is also prime minister, joined party leaders and delegates in a cake-cutting ceremony during the event. PKR was established in 1999 following the reform movement triggered by Anwar's dismissal as deputy prime minister in 1998, with Parti Keadilan Nasional serving as the primary political vehicle.

items.title: University leaders welcome Auku abolishment, call for balance between freedom, accountability
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's plan to abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) has been welcomed by public university leaders as a transformative step towards strengthening institutional autonomy, governance and academic freedom. They said the move demonstrated the government's commitment to comprehensive reform of the higher education ecosystem, while stressing that any new legal framework must strike a clear balance between freedom and accountability. [[nid:1512312]] Meanwhile, International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) rector Professor Emeritus Datuk Seri Dr Osman Bakar said the move would give students greater scope to develop mature thinking, strengthen leadership potential and participate constructively in society.

items.title: DAP veteran leader urges party to speak up on government issues
items.summary: She said that while DAP's ministers had a strong record of reform, the party could not ignore deeper problems. She said corruption scandals had escalated despite DAP's pledge to eradicate graft. Where is DAP?

items.title: DAP votes on staying in unity government [WATCH]
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Thousands of DAP delegates began casting secret ballots about 1pm today on whether the party should remain in the Federal Government for the rest of the current parliamentary term. The outcome will determine whether DAP ministers and deputy ministers will remain in the cabinet until the end of the current term, following the party's recent string of state election setbacks. DAP lost all eight seats it contested in the Sabah election last November before suffering further losses in the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections.

items.title: Malaysian Qualifications Agency says abolition of AUKU cannot be taken lightly, urges clear guidelines
items.summary: Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA) chief executive officer Prof Datuk Dr Mohammad Shatar Sabran said any changes to the higher education legal framework must be made comprehensively and carefully to avoid gaps in terms of regulations, governance and institutional monitoring. He said the higher education system needs clear guidelines and procedures to ensure that university management and administration remain orderly and accountable. “Any decision regarding the abolition of AUKU must be preceded by a comprehensive approach as recommended by the Ministry of Higher Education (KPT), including a comprehensive assessment of the implications of changes to the higher education ecosystem.

items.title: Fuziah: PH reform agenda still incomplete after nearly four years
items.summary: MELAKA: The reform agenda has yet to be fully realised despite Pakatan Harapan leading the government for nearly four years because few Cabinet members truly understand it, PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Saleh said today. Fuziah acknowledged that voices remained loud in pointing out that many institutional changes promised by PH had yet to be implemented. Also present was PKR president and PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

items.title: Ex-cop fined RM4,500 for threatening to kill wife
items.summary: The accused, Muhd Sirrul Akmal Rasali, 43, entered the plea after the charge was read before magistrate Wan Ashrul Afham Mohamad Azmi. According to the charge, the accused was alleged to have committed criminal intimidation against his 42-year-old wife by threatening to kill her, causing her to feel fearful, at Kampung Semat Jal, Wakaf Bharu, near here at 9am on Aug 8. Earlier, Megat Asyraf requested an appropriate sentence for the accused.

items.title: North Korea's Kim tells Putin he is 'proud' of strong ties
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un told Russian President Vladimir Putin he was "proud" of their countries' strong ties, state media reported Sunday, after providing military support for Moscow's war against Ukraine. Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, North Korea has become a key ally of the Kremlin, sending troops to support Moscow's war effort in return for economic benefits and military technology, analysts say. DPRK is the acronym for the North's official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar seeks stronger governance rules for state-owned entities
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he will soon bring a proposed law on state-owned enterprises to the Cabinet to ensure all government-owned entities are subject to clear and consistent governance rules. Anwar said the government's push to strengthen governance would also extend beyond issues involving Tabung Haji and the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda). "He said, 'Continue with all the agencies that have problems'," Anwar said.

items.title: Sarawak skies turn grey, DOE warns haze plumes from Kalimantan push API into danger zone
items.summary: Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said two other areas, Samarahan and Kuching, recorded API readings of 155 and 132, respectively, believed to be due to haze smoke moving in from various directions. She said 65 other areas recorded moderate air quality levels. Azuri Azizah said moderate smoke plumes were observed over southern and western Kalimantan, while light, localised smoke plumes were detected in southern and central Sumatra.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution made PKR’s de facto number two as Nurul Izzah steps down
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution will take over the duties of PKR’s deputy president after incumbent Nurul Izzah Anwar announced she would “take leave”. Prime Minister and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the handover at the party’s congress here this afternoon, where Nurul Izzah also gave a parting speech that called on the party to unite and galvanise its “differences” as a form of strength. Anwar also gave full authority to PKR vice president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari to direct the party’s election campaigns, a move he suggested would streamline preparations and strategies to avoid confusion in the chain of command.

items.title: At DAP congress, most delegates back staying in Anwar govt, urge faster reforms
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP delegates debating whether the party should remain in the federal government today have largely backed staying until the end of the current term, while urging Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to accelerate reforms promised to Malaysians. Speaking during the party’s national congress here, several delegates argued that leaving the unity government now would amount to abandoning voters and handing political advantage to rival parties. Perak delegate and Sitiawan assemblyman Jason Ng Thien Yeong said his position was simple: DAP should remain in the government until the end of the term.

items.title: Aminuddin says he’ll take responsibility, ready to quit PKR Negeri Sembilan role after polls loss
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Former Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has expressed his readiness to step down as chairman of the Negeri Sembilan State Leadership Council (MPN) of Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) following the recent state election. Aminuddin said he agreed with the demands of six PKR branch leaders in the state who are urging the party leadership to reassess its position after PKR only won two of the 15 state assembly seats contested. “I also take note of the demands of the six Negeri Sembilan branch leaders who want me to take responsibility for the defeat.

items.title: At DAP congress, Sangeet urges rethink of ties with Anwar, says PM has divided coalition, empowered Umno
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — Wanita DAP legal bureau chief Sangeet Kaur Deo today called on the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) to reassess its relationship with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, ahead of a vote at the national congress on whether DAP should remain in the federal government. While favouring DAP’s continued participation in the federal government, Sangeet said the current coalition arrangement under Anwar had failed to unite its partners. She said the party could not ignore growing racial divisions and corruption-related scandals during its time in the federal government, warning that its silence on these issues had affected public confidence.

items.title: Gobind says DAP must chase reforms Unity partners can deliver, not manifesto wish‑lists
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP must use the results of recent state elections as a basis to reassess its direction and ensure the party remains relevant in the country’s evolving political landscape, its national chairman Gobind Singh Deo said. He said this was important after three and a half years of DAP’s participation in the Unity Government, allowing the party to review its achievements and shortcomings during the period before charting its future course. But the results have prompted us to reconsider how we should move forward,” he said in his welcoming speech at the DAP Party Conference 2026 at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here today.

items.title: No MACC arrest, just rumours: Abdul Azeez’s son rebuts social media buzz over Tabung Haji RCI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — The son of former Baling Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has dismissed claims that have gone viral on social media that his father was arrested by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) last night. Mohamed Khairul Azman Abdul Azeez, through a post on Facebook today, said his father is currently at their residence and resting, thus denying unfounded reports regarding his arrest in connection with the Tabung Haji Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report. Rumours about the arrest of Abdul Azeez, who is also the former chairman of Tabung Haji, began to spread widely on several social media platforms since late last night.

items.title: Anwar launches Temu Fikrah, PKR Youth’s manifesto‑meets‑manual for courage, creativity and Madani governance
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Prime Minister and Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched Temu Fikrah , a publication produced by the PKR Youth wing (AMK) in conjunction with the PKR National Congress 2026. The 113-page publication, authored by AMK chief Muhammad Kamil Ahmad Munim and AMK executive committee member Ashraf Ahmad Hadi, outlines the movement’s new thinking on addressing contemporary challenges. In the foreword, Anwar described the publication as timely, coinciding with the adoption of the Malaysia Madani concept as the intellectual framework and strategic direction for the nation’s administration.

items.title: PKR’s 27‑year struggle isn’t about power, Zaliha says it’s about changing how Malaysia is run
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Becoming a government is not the end of the Reformasi struggle but rather a real test to prove the courage and wisdom to implement change, said Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) vice president Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa. She said the reformasi struggle led by PKR for 27 years should not be seen simply as an effort to take over the country’s administration, but rather aimed at changing the way the country is governed. “Implementing reform also requires wisdom.

items.title: DAP’s destiny on the table as Anthony Loke leaves Unity decision to Putrajaya delegates
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — The DAP Party Conference today is the appropriate forum to decide whether the party should remain in or withdraw from the Unity Government, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke. Therefore, the delegates have to make a collective decision for the party. He said this when delivering his policy speech at the 2026 DAP Party Conference at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here.

items.title: Loke apologises to DAP delegates for losing Chennah in Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke today apologised to party delegates for failing to retain Chennah, a seat he had held for three consecutive terms since 2013, in the recent Negeri Sembilan state election. “I felt saddened that as the party secretary-general I was unable to retain the seat in the recent Negeri Sembilan state election and for that I would like to apologise to all the delegates for this defeat. In the recent Negeri Sembilan state election, Loke lost to MCA’s John Kong Choon, who won the seat with a majority of 688 votes.

items.title: Asyraf Wajdi suspends MARA staff after eight students allege sexual harassment misconduct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) has immediately suspended a member of its staff following allegations of sexual harassment involving at least eight students at a MARA educational institution. MARA chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the action was taken to facilitate a thorough investigation to be conducted without interference from the parties involved. He said the matter came to light after receiving direct messages from several students claiming to be victims, prompting him to order MARA management to take immediate action.

items.title: DAP backs Anwar ‘100 per cent’ on AUKU repeal, Loke says reforms must go further
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP today said it will support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim “100 per cent” in abolishing the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU), but stressed that the same spirit must be extended to other promised reforms. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said education reform should go beyond the abolition of AUKU and focus on ensuring equal access to higher education for all Malaysians, regardless of their racial background. “AUKU is one component, but what is more important in education reform is to ensure equal opportunities for higher education for all Malaysians, regardless of their racial background.

items.title: Fadhlina tells PKR members not to wait for Parliament dissolution to prepare for polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Wanita chief Fadhlina Sidek has urged party members to remain election-ready at all times and not wait for Parliament to be dissolved before making preparations. “We must strengthen PKR so that whoever is with us, we remain strong. Whoever leaves us, we remain strong.

items.title: Control the media? We even give them massage chairs, Fahmi tells PKR congress
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today suggested that PKR will not resort to punitive measures against members of the press, even as some in the party believe its rivals are winning the messaging battle by fighting dirty. Speaking to party delegates, Fahmi suggested that PKR had lost the communications war, leading voters to “vote over emotions instead of performance”. Fahmi said instead that his party was treating the press much better than previous governments, joking that it even provided massage chairs to reporters covering the party’s congress.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain, strong winds in Perlis, Melaka, Sarawak, other areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas in the Peninsula and Sarawak until 1pm today. The weather warning also involves Kuantan, Pekan and Jerantut in Pahang; Sepang and Kuala Langat in Selangor; Port Dickson, Seremban, Rembau, Kuala Pilah and Tampin in Negeri Sembilan; and Tangkak and Muar in Johor. For Sarawak, the same forecast was issued for the areas of Mukah, Selangau, Sibu, Sarikei, Maradong, Bintulu, Kapit, Bukit Mabong and Subis in Miri.

items.title: Rafizi: Bersama names 15 candidates early to give Melaka voters time to assess
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) has announced candidates for 15 of the 28 seats in the Melaka state legislative assembly, becoming the first party to unveil its candidates ahead of the state election, The Star reported. The party’s line-up includes Dr Muhamad Solehin Saleh, 40, the elder brother of Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, who will contest Bemban. Bersama co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said the early announcement was made before the state assembly is dissolved, allowing voters more time to assess the candidates and their plans.

items.title: PAS wants Selangor to be launchpad for toppling PH, says Sanusi
items.summary: “If PH falls in Selangor, PH will fall at the federal level,” he was quoted as saying at a Selangor PAS election machinery gathering at the Selangor PAS complex here last night. What has PH achieved? PH and BN subsequently formed the state government.

items.title: Student loses RM29,000 after scammers pose as cops, threaten arrest over money laundering
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 16 — Police arrested three local men, aged between 32 and 45, in five raids across Kuala Lumpur and Selangor on Thursday for allegedly being involved in an online scam syndicate. Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspects were arrested at various locations in Petaling Jaya, Kelana Jaya, Ulu Kelang, Damansara and Kuala Lumpur. He said the arrests followed a police report lodged by a 22-year-old student who lost RM28,999 after being deceived by individuals posing as law enforcement officers and claiming that he was involved in money laundering.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin graces Perak Merdeka Month programme with 214,095 student entries
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 16 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, today graced a programme to instil the spirit of loyalty to the Ruler and country in conjunction with the Perak-level 2026 Merdeka Month at Bangunan Perak Darul Ridzuan here last night. Also in attendance were the Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, accompanied by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh. Perak Education Department director Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar, in his royal address, said this year’s programme recorded an encouraging turnout, with 214,095 entries involving 83.6 per cent of primary and secondary school students in Perak.

items.title: ESSCom chief: Claims of armed men entering Semporna, Lahad Datu baseless
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Claims of a group of armed men entering Semporna and Lahad Datu, Sabah that went viral on social media are fake, Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCom) commander Datuk Victor Sanjos said. Victor said ESSCom always monitors and implements security control, especially in waters and strategic locations in the East Sabah Security Zone, adding that any information about security threats should be channelled to the authorities for further action and confirmation. — Bernama

items.title: Police probe Facebook account owner over alleged seditious, insulting post against royals, govt
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 15 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) is conducting an investigation into the owner of the Facebook account ‘Ahmad Mu’min’ following a post, which is suspected to contain elements of sedition and insult against the royal institution, the Malaysian government and the PDRM. Kemaman district police chief Supt Mohd Razi Mohd Rosli said the investigation under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 is being conducted after a report was received from a 29-year-old man at 11.14 am yesterday. “The police will investigate the identity of the account owner and subsequently conduct an investigation according to legal procedures,” he said in a statement yesterday.
